exact_statement: For every n>=2 and nonempty physical support U of mass p on the uniform cube, f=1-2*1_U, and original actual connected-component labels, max over nonempty proper blocks A of W_A/(|A|p) equals max_i Inf_i(f)/(2p). Thus the sufficient criterion W_A>=|A|p/2 admits a proper block iff some Inf_i(f)>=p. Let h=H(X|L), X uniform on U, and b=h-n+I(f)/(2p)>=0. Given the prior universal actual-block bound L_A<=4|A|p+a I_A, a=2/ln2+4/(e ln2), a least-essential-dimension K-violation with K>a, D=H-KI>0 and actual singleton child reserves S_i>=0 satisfies h>=n-2n/(K-a)+b+(nD+sum_i S_i)/(2p(K-a)). At K>=4+a both sign sets therefore have a component larger than 2^(n/2), and every proper block fails the sufficient fiber criterion on either sign. This is a limitation of this admission rule, not a disproof of FEI.
hypotheses: n>=2, finite uniform physical cube, nonempty support p>0; f is an actual Boolean sign
L is the original actual connected-component label; labels are retained after restriction
Entropy is in bits; Inf_i uses the usual Boolean flip probability
The critical corollary assumes K>a and least essential dimension among actual K-violations
For the critical corollary use the stated prior transfer/row upper bound; child deficits are actual and retained

proof_dependencies.used_scope: Only universal terminal-inclusive block bound (7)/(9); the admission identity itself is independent
